title: ACT Reading: Four Passages, Fast
summary: The ACT Reading passages, why speed is the challenge, and how to answer from the text under time pressure.

nodes.label: Passage types
nodes.note: Literary, social science, humanities, natural science

nodes.label: Answer from the text
nodes.note: Every answer is provable in the passage

nodes.label: Line references
nodes.note: Use them to jump to the spot

chunks.heading: Four passage types
chunks.body: Reading has passages across **literary narrative, social science, humanities, and natural science**. The content is unfamiliar on purpose — you're not expected to know the topic, only to **find and understand what the passage says**.
chunks.realExample: A natural-science passage about ocean currents doesn't test your science knowledge — every answer is about what THIS passage states, so read it as new information.
chunks.memoryHook: Four passage types, all unfamiliar. You answer from the passage, not prior knowledge.

chunks.heading: Every answer is in the text
chunks.body: Correct answers are **directly supported by the passage**; wrong ones are true-in-general, too extreme, or twist a detail. If you can't **point to the lines** that prove a choice, it's probably a trap.
chunks.realExample: 'The author suggests…' → find the sentence that backs it. An option that sounds sensible but isn't stated is the classic wrong answer.
chunks.memoryHook: Underline the proof. No proof in the text = not the answer.

chunks.heading: Speed is the real challenge
chunks.body: You have **limited time per passage**, so **don't read every word slowly**. Skim for the main idea and structure, then **go to the passage for each question** — most detail questions send you to a specific spot rather than needing a full re-read.
chunks.realExample: Read the passage briskly for gist, then let each question's keyword or line reference point you to the exact place to check — targeted, not exhaustive, reading.
chunks.memoryHook: Skim for gist, then hunt per question. Reading every word slowly runs out the clock.

chunks.heading: Use line references and keywords
chunks.body: Many questions give a **line number or a keyword** — jump straight there and read a little around it. Answer the detail from that spot rather than from memory, and **don't leave any question blank** (no penalty).
chunks.realExample: 'In line 24, "current" most nearly means…' → read lines 23–25 and pick the meaning that fits the context, not the dictionary default.
chunks.memoryHook: Line reference? Jump there, read around it, answer from the text. Never blank.

recall.q: What are the four ACT Reading passage types?
recall.a: Literary narrative, social science, humanities, and natural science.

recall.q: What makes an ACT Reading answer correct?
recall.a: It's directly supported by lines in the passage — not merely true in general.

recall.q: Why is speed the main challenge in ACT Reading?
recall.a: Time per passage is tight, so you must skim for gist and target the passage per question rather than reading every word slowly.

recall.q: How should you use line references and keywords?
recall.a: Jump to that spot, read a little around it, and answer the detail from the text rather than from memory.

recall.q: Should you leave a Reading question blank if short on time?
recall.a: No — there's no penalty, so guess on every remaining question.
